---
title: "About Mithril Metrics"
---

*Mithril Metrics* publishes short, reproducible case studies on agri-food, climate and rural
policy. Each one starts from a current policy debate, asks one narrow empirical question, and
answers it with public data in about four hours.

## How each case is built

- **Public data only.** Every number traces to a named dataset and access date.
- **One question, one answer.** The bottom line comes first; caveats are stated plainly.
- **Methods from production and resource economics:** production frontiers, productivity and
  efficiency measurement, water economics and governance, risk and fat tails, panel and causal-ML econometrics.
- **Reproducible.** All code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/Mithril-Metrics/mithril-metrics.github.io)
  and runs end to end in R.
- **Neutral.** Policy implications are written as trade-offs, not recommendations.

## People

[**Juan Pablo Henao**](people/juan-pablo-henao.qmd): applied environmental economist, Chair of
Agricultural Production and Resource Economics, Technical University of Munich; formerly FAO.
Water pricing and governance, sustainable productivity, optimisation and efficiency analysis.

[**Pietro Sala**](people/pietro-sala.qmd): applied economist, Chair of Agricultural Production
and Resource Economics, Technical University of Munich. Production and efficiency analysis,
eco-efficiency, climate risk, water and the WEFE nexus.
